predecessors.name: Bijapur Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Bijapuri forts and districts Shivaji took from Torna (1647) to Ponda, Karwar and Kolhapur (1675); the Karnataka conquests of 1677 also came from Bijapuri holdings

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: the Peshwa's territories 'annexed into the Bombay Presidency', Bundelkhand as the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories, the northern part of Nagpur, and the districts ceded in 1803-1805

successors.name: Gwalior State
successors.text: Shinde's lands, which became 'a princely state acknowledging British control'

successors.name: Indore State
successors.text: Holkar's lands, 'a subsidiary princely state under a British Resident' after the Treaty of Mandeswar (6 January 1818)

successors.name: Kingdom of Nagpur
successors.text: Bhonsle's lands, 'a princely state' under British guardianship with the northern portion annexed into the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories

successors.name: Satara State
successors.text: 'The Maharaja was restored as ruler of a princely state' at Satara (annexed 1848)

ledger.x: 1674: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.
April 1675: Shivaji takes Ponda from Bijapur ('capturing the Bijapuri forts of Ponda (April 1675), Karwar (mid-year), and Kolhapur (July)').
July 1675: Kolhapur and Karwar pass from Bijapur to the Marathas.
1677: Shivaji invades the Karnataka and seizes Vellore and Gingee.
26 November 1677: Shivaji defeats his half-brother Venkoji and takes his Mysore-plateau holdings.
1680: the Mughal-Maratha (Deccan) wars begin.
1689: Sambhaji is captured (1 February) and executed (21 March); Rajaram takes the court south to Jinji, 'Jinji: 1689-1698 (de facto)' in the infobox.
January 1698: Jinji falls to the Mughals; the page says Jinji 'fell in January 1698'.
1700: Rajaram dies at Sinhagad (March 1700) and Tarabai rules for her son; the infobox gives 'Satara: 1700-1818 (royal seat)'.
April 1700: Satara surrenders to Aurangzeb.
1706: the Mughals start to leave Maratha land.
1707: the Maratha house divides.
21 February 1707: Aurangzeb dies and the long Mughal war ends de facto.
16 November 1713: Balaji Vishwanath is appointed Peshwa.
1719: the Marathas march to Delhi and depose Farrukhsiyar, and Shahu is granted possession of Shivaji's 1680 territory.

1728: the Peshwa's seat is Poona (infobox 'Poona: 1728-1818'); the same year Baji Rao I beat the Nizam at Palkhed (28 February in this page, 25 February in the Baji Rao I page) and the Nizam signed the Treaty of Mungi Shevgaon on 6 March recognising Shahu and the Maratha tax rights.
1730: a Maratha force under Chimaji Appa goes into Gujarat ('sent a Maratha force under Chimaji Appa there in 1730'); at Dabhoi in 1731 Baji Rao I beat the rebel Maratha Trimbak Rao Dabhade.
1731: Chhatrasal leaves the Marathas a third of Bundelkhand.
25 September 1736: the Siddis of Janjira are shut in.
1738: Gujarat is Maratha.
1738: Gujarat enters the Maratha shape.
1738: the Marathas attack Bassein.
7 January 1738: the Treaty of Bhopal gives Malwa to the Marathas.
1739: Khargone and Handia are ceded.
1740: Raghuji Bhonsle's army enters the Carnatic.
14 March 1741: Trichinopoly surrenders and the Carnatic expedition ends.
April 1742: Bhaskar Ram's Marathas invade Bengal through Orissa.
1751: the Subarnarekha becomes the frontier.
1752: Orissa is formally incorporated.
August 1757: Raghunath Rao takes Delhi.
8 May 1758: Peshawar falls to the Marathas in the Afghan-Maratha war (infobox 8 March 1758 - 14 January 1761).
3 January 1760: Sadashivrao Bhau beats Salabat Jung at Udgir.
August 1760: Delhi is retaken.
14 January 1761: the Marathas lose the Third Battle of Panipat and the northwest.
January 1761: Delhi passes out of Maratha hands after Panipat.
Early 1771: Mahadaji Shinde recaptures Delhi ('Mahadaji Shinde recaptured Delhi in early 1771').

1 March 1776: the Treaty of Purandar annuls the Treaty of Surat (6 March 1775, Raghunathrao ceded 'Salsette and Bassein' and part of the Surat and Bharuch revenues) but 'the revenues of Salsette and Bharuch districts were retained by the British'.

wars.name: Mughal-Maratha Wars
wars.outcome: Aurangzeb took Bijapur by September 1686, captured Sambhaji on 1 February 1689, took Jinji in January 1698 and Satara in April 1700, but died on 21 February 1707 with the Marathas under Tarabai raiding across the Narmada; Shahu was released and the Maratha…

wars.name: Battle of Palkhed
wars.outcome: Baji Rao I beat the Nizam on 25 or 28 February 1728; by the Treaty of Mungi Shevgaon (6 March) the Nizam recognised Shahu and the Maratha tax rights in the Deccan.

wars.name: Maratha-Siddi wars of Janjira
wars.outcome: The 1733 treaty left the Siddis Janjira, Anjanvel, Gowalkot and Underi; the peace of 25 September 1736 confined them to Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel.

wars.name: Maratha conquest of Malwa and Battle of Bhopal
wars.outcome: Deputy governor of Malwa from 4 March 1736; Delhi outskirts 28 March 1737; Bhopal in December 1737; the treaty of 7 January 1738 ceded Malwa and Rs 5,000,000.

wars.name: Maratha invasions of Bengal
wars.outcome: Six expeditions (Maratha Empire page: 1741-1748; the Bengal page covers 1742-1752) ended with the 1751 treaty: Rs 1,200,000 a year chauth, the Subarnarekha as boundary, Orissa incorporated in 1752.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Carnatic
wars.outcome: Raghuji Bhonsle beat and killed Dost Ali at Damalcherry in 1740, Arcot was taken, Trichinopoly surrendered on 14 March 1741.

wars.name: Afghan-Maratha War (Third Battle of Panipat)
wars.outcome: Peshawar fell to the Marathas on 8 May 1758; the Marathas lost the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761 and the north-west.

wars.name: Battle of Udgir
wars.outcome: Sadashivrao Bhau beat Salabat Jung on 3 January 1760; the Nizam surrendered territory worth 60 lakhs.

wars.name: Maratha-Mysore wars
wars.outcome: Madhavrao I crossed the Krishna in 1767 and beat Hyder Ali at Sira and Madgiri; the infobox gives August 1768 - April 1787 and the Treaty of Gajendragad of April 1787.

wars.name: First Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Inconclusive; the Treaty of Salbai (17 May 1782) returned the territory captured in the war, the British keeping Salsette.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: British victory: Deogaon (17 December 1803) and Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803) ceded Cuttack, Haryana, the Doab, Delhi-Agra, parts of Bundelkhand, Broach and Ahmadnagar; Rajghat (24 December 1805) took Tonk, Rampura and Bundi from Holkar.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: The Peshwa's territories were annexed into the Bombay Presidency, the Bhonsle lost most of Nagpur, Holkar and Shinde became British subsidiaries; Satara was restored as a princely state; Asirgarh fell on 9 April 1819.

certainty.note: Hill forts and raided districts: the pages give forts and cities, not boundaries.
Chauth and sphere-of-influence land is not territory.
The British treaty cessions of 1803, 1805 and 1817-1818 name districts and are sharp; the lines between the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle remain soft.
